display.headline: How you come across before you say anything
display.body: Analytical, service-oriented and precision-focused. Systems, routines and quality standards matter deeply.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

display.headline: What you are actually driving at
display.body: Core identity seeks variety, ideas and exchange.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

display.headline: How you settle yourself
display.body: Emotional rhythm is detached and objective, preferring conceptual distance.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

display.headline: Your default way of deciding
display.body: 3 of your seven main planets sit in air signs, which is enough to set a house style. Under pressure, and with no time to think it through, you will think a decision through out loud, and change your mind when the argument changes. That is worth knowing mostly so you can tell when it is the right instinct and when it is just the loudest one.
display.tension: What you are drawn to does not match how you actually operate. Your momentum is air, but what attracts you runs fire, so the things you want and the way you go about getting them can quietly work against each other.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 25 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Dominant element: Air, carried by 3 of the seven classical planets.

display.headline: Where your chart is most crowded
display.body: More of your chart is stacked into one area of life than any other: creativity, romance and children. Concentration like this tends to make a theme unavoidable rather than optional -- it is where the repeated events, the recurring lessons and the disproportionate share of your attention end up going.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: House 5 in Capricorn carries Saturn, Rahu.

display.headline: The engine your life actually runs on
display.body: The planet in charge of your whole chart is Mercury, and where it sits decides where your life keeps steering: beliefs, wisdom and long-distance journeys. Of everything in a chart, this is the single clearest signal for what you will end up organising your years around, whether or not you chose it deliberately.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 1 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Mercury rules Virgo and is placed in Taurus, house 9.

display.headline: Where you go looking for reassurance
display.body: Your attention keeps returning to service, routines and health whenever you need to feel steady. This is less about what you value in principle and more about where you instinctively go when something has knocked you off balance and you want the ground back under you.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

display.headline: What you are hungry for, and what you are done with
display.body: One end of this axis pulls you toward creativity, romance and children with an appetite that rarely feels fully satisfied. The other asks you to loosen your grip on community, networks and long goals, which is usually the area you are already good at and can hide in. The pull and the release are the same mechanism.
display.tension: Both ends misbehave when they run unsupervised. Chasing too hard makes urgency outrun judgement; letting go too easily looks like maturity but is often just avoidance wearing better clothes.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Rahu in Capricorn, house 5; Ketu in Cancer, house 11.

display.headline: Your life happens out loud
display.body: 3 of your planets sit on the four corners of the chart -- the positions tied to self, home, partnership and public standing. Charts weighted this way tend to produce visible, eventful lives that respond quickly to decisive action, and respond just as quickly to indecision.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 23 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Planets in kendras: Sun, Mars, Jupiter.

display.headline: Saturn is on home ground
display.body: Saturn sits in a sign it governs, so your discipline, patience and relationship with limits behaves consistently rather than in bursts. This is not the most dramatic placement in a chart, but it is one of the most trustworthy: what it promises on a good day is roughly what it delivers on an average one.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 14 of every 100 charts

display.headline: Sun is in the one position where it works hardest for you
display.body: Sun sits in the part of your chart where classical astrology says it gains directional strength -- the position it is most at home in, whichever sign it happens to be in. That tends to make your sense of self and the authority you carry unusually effective and easy to reach for: it is one of the tools you use without thinking, and other people often notice it before you do.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Sun in house 10 (Gemini): dig bala, full directional strength.

display.headline: Saturn does its best work on the second pass
display.body: Saturn was moving backwards in the sky when you were born -- retrograde, in astrology's term. Classical texts treat a retrograde planet as strong but unconventional: your discipline, patience and relationship with limits tends to work inward first, revisiting and revising before it commits, and to find its own route rather than the expected one. What looks like hesitation from the outside is usually thoroughness.
display.tension: The trap is mistaking the review for the result. At some point the revision has to be finished and put in front of people, even if it could still be improved.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 36 of every 100 charts

display.headline: How your working life is built
display.body: Communication-centered career path. Journalism, writing, teaching, marketing, or trading leverage your intellectual agility.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 10th house sign: Gemini. Lord Mercury placed in house 9 in Taurus.

claims.label: 10th lord placement
claims.detail: The 6th, 8th and 12th are the houses of effort, disruption and loss.

display.headline: Your work is where people find you
display.body: Sun, Jupiter sit directly in the part of your chart that governs profession and public standing, which pushes their qualities straight into how you are seen at work. Careers with this signature tend to be less separable from identity than most -- what you do and who you are keep collapsing into the same answer.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 13 of every 100 charts

display.headline: What you are actually looking for in a partner
display.body: Romantic, empathic and spiritually connected in love. You seek a soulmate bond, creative expression, and emotional transcendence.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 9 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 7th house sign: Pisces. Lord Jupiter in house 10 (Gemini).

display.headline: How you show affection, as opposed to how you feel it
display.body: Venus is the part of a chart that governs attraction and how care actually gets expressed. In Aries it runs through fire habits, which shapes what reads as love when you give it -- and, more usefully, explains why affection you offered sincerely has sometimes not landed as affection at all.
display.tension: How you express desire and what you want from commitment are made of different material -- fire against water. Left unexamined this shows up as choosing people you are drawn to over people you would actually be well matched with.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 8 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Venus at 24.91 deg in Aries, house 8.

display.headline: Romance and creativity run on the same circuit
display.body: Saturn, Rahu occupy the part of your chart that handles play, romance and creative output. These tend to move together for you: periods where you are making something are usually periods where you are more open to being pursued, and creative droughts and romantic ones often arrive in the same month.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 12 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: 5th house in Capricorn with Saturn, Rahu.

display.headline: Passion in your relationships needs a steering wheel
display.body: Mars -- drive, desire and the appetite for conflict -- sits in one of the six positions the Indian matchmaking tradition watches most closely for intensity in partnership. It shows up in a large share of charts, which is the first thing worth knowing about it: it describes a temperament, not a fate. In practice it adds heat and speed to relationships -- attraction to intensity, quick flare-ups, a strong need for directness -- and it goes best with a partner who has comparable fire, or who is not rattled by yours.
display.tension: Here Mars sits right on the partnership axis, so arguments can escalate faster than you mean them to. The skill that pays off most is a pause: the hard thing said an hour later lands better than the same thing said now.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 39 of every 100 charts

evidence.technical_note: Mars in house 7 (Pisces, neutral): kuja dosha from the lagna, not cancelled by own sign or exaltation.

display.headline: Teachers and beliefs carry more weight for you than average
display.body: The part of your chart dealing with belief, higher learning and long-range good fortune is occupied rather than empty. Charts like this tend to have identifiable turning points attached to a particular teacher, a particular book, or a period abroad -- influence arriving from outside your existing world rather than from inside it.
display.rarity_label: Shows up in about 33 of every 100 charts
